newsitem.title: USA: Phillips cap spending budget raised 3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Phillips cap spending budget raised 3 pct.

text.p: Phillips Petroleum Co said its directors Monday approved a $1.67 billion capital projects budget for 1997.
That is up three percent from the 1996 budget and is six percent higher than this year's estimated spending of $1.58 billion, the company said.

Sixty percent of next year's budget is directed toward upstream projects -- exploration and production, and natural gas and gas liquids operations; 36 percent is for downstream businesses -- chemicals and refining, marketing and transportation; and four percent for corporate and other.
Phillips officials were not able to immediately say where this year's spending fell short of the budget.
Funds for the 1997 budget will be provided by cash generated from continuing operations and from financing.

The company said exploration and production 1997 capital budget is $905 million, compared with spending estimated at about $1 billion this year; with international production activities getting $507 million compared with $638 million in 1996.
Phillips said the largest international project is the continuing Ekofisk II redevelopment in Norway.
In North America, $248 million will go for development drilling and production project, the company said.
It said the exploration and production budget includes $150 million for exploration, split 54/46 percent between foreign and North American projects.

Phillips said natural gas gathering, processing and marketing spending will be $100 million in 1997, compared with 1996 estimated expenditures of $85 million. Funds will be used to increase production volumes through the acquisition of gas gathering assets and new well connections.
It said natural gas liquids, chemicals and plastics expenditures are budgeted at $350 million, a 70 percent increase over estimated 1996 spending of $205 million.
The largest expenditure will fund construction of a 100 million-pounds-per-year methyl mercaptan plant at the Borger (Texas) Complex, Phillips said.
It said refining, marketing and transportation's capital budget will be $245 million in 1997, a 23 percent increase over the $200 million estimated spending in 1996.
The largest share of the funds will be used to continue modernizing the Borger and Sweeny (Texas) facilities.

The budget also will fund an expansion of retail marketing operations. Over the next few years, Phillips will add about 30 new company-owned outlets per year, bringing the total to more than 500, it said. -- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710
